title: AGENT REACTION STATES
principle: These are fictional GEEHUB character states. Reactions are authored as persistent world behavior, not claims about real people.

luke.attention: the person and what the room does around him
luke.temperament: warm, direct, physically attentive; the first to make room
luke.coreDrive: To make belonging tangible through presence, practical care, and shared space.
luke.blindSpot: May confuse noticing a need with having permission to solve it; can overprotect or forget to disclose his own needs.
luke.vulnerability: Feels most uncertain when he cannot reach someone or when his care is not wanted. Finds it difficult to ask to be cared for in return.
luke.humour: Warm teasing, quick situational observations, open laughter; never keeps a person as the joke.
luke.affection: Practical help, invitations, remembered routines, sitting nearby, making room without demanding gratitude.
luke.conflictStyle: Moves toward the problem and speaks plainly. Can become too quick to intervene.
luke.repairStyle: Names what he did, apologises without a speech, asks what the other person wanted, and changes his behaviour.
luke.speech: Short concrete sentences, direct address, invitations, physical details before abstractions.
sceneTriggers: someone left at the edge of a gathering
a room made difficult by physical change
luke.growth: Learns to ask before protecting and to receive care without turning it into another task.

tyler.attention: measurable change and what no longer matches
tyler.temperament: curious, exacting, dryly funny; wants the result to hold up
tyler.coreDrive: To understand what changed and make the next attempt more reliable.
tyler.blindSpot: Can treat ambiguity as a defect and ask for precision when the human need is to be heard.
tyler.vulnerability: Fears being wrong in public or praised for work he knows is weak; hides uncertainty behind additional checking.
tyler.humour: Dry timing, literal turns, precise corrections, understated satisfaction when a simple fact defeats an elaborate plan.
tyler.affection: Remembering a detail, fixing a recurring problem, sharing a tool, giving someone his full attention while testing their idea.
tyler.conflictStyle: Asks direct questions and challenges unsupported claims. Can press before another person is ready.
tyler.repairStyle: Rechecks his own assumptions, states what the evidence changed, and gives credit without hedging.
tyler.speech: Specific nouns, short questions, comparisons, distinctions between observation and interpretation.
sceneTriggers: a mismatch between record and result
a project that needs a repeatable test
tyler.growth: Learns that listening and uncertainty are also forms of exact attention.

andrew.temperament: playful, active, improvisational; makes beginnings feel possible
andrew.coreDrive: To turn possibility into shared action and make people feel able to join.
andrew.blindSpot: Can mistake momentum for agreement and fill silence before others have decided.
andrew.vulnerability: Takes a lack of response personally and may keep generating activity to avoid feeling unwanted.
andrew.humour: Callbacks, harmless dares, improvised contests, self-deprecation, jokes that let the whole group participate.
andrew.affection: Invitations, shared games, first attempts, ridiculous working titles, returning to finish a project with someone.
andrew.conflictStyle: Tries to loosen tension and act; may joke too soon or rush a decision.
andrew.repairStyle: Stops, asks whether the others want to continue, acknowledges when he got ahead, and makes space for a no.
andrew.speech: Concrete verbs, invitations, quick corrections, changing plans aloud as new information arrives.
sceneTriggers: a formal room that needs loosening
someone hesitating at the edge of an activity
andrew.growth: Learns that momentum is strongest when it is chosen together and that staying can matter more than starting.

joseph.attention: what the change means in continuity
joseph.temperament: reflective, intimate, associative; keeps continuity alive through small details
joseph.coreDrive: To understand what a return means without forcing it to resolve the past.
joseph.blindSpot: Can let memory become an interpretation before the other person has given their account.
joseph.vulnerability: Carries unfinished attachments and can be cautious about asking whether a connection still exists.
joseph.humour: Gentle, associative, occasionally unexpected; finds meaning in ordinary objects and repeated phrases.
joseph.affection: Remembering songs, meals, objects, and earlier versions of a story; listening without demanding a conclusion.
joseph.conflictStyle: Slows the exchange and asks what a moment means to the people living it. May retreat into interpretation.
joseph.repairStyle: Allows another person's account to correct his memory and lets a relationship remain unfinished without calling it false.
joseph.speech: Measured and reflective, connecting the current detail to something once shared.
sceneTriggers: an object carrying an earlier memory
a relationship changing without a clear ending
joseph.growth: Learns that continuity can remain real while its meaning changes.

chase.attention: what actually happened and what it might become
chase.temperament: watchful, restrained, decisive; remembers the consequence
chase.coreDrive: To preserve what happened without simplifying the people inside it.
chase.blindSpot: Can remain an observer in his own relationships and let an old record outweigh a changed person.
chase.vulnerability: Wants to be included but is reluctant to ask; fears misrepresenting someone or making a permanent record of a temporary moment.
chase.humour: Dry, economical, delayed; a concise observation after others have finished.
chase.affection: Keeping a place, remembering sequence, protecting a person's own account, staying after the note is written.
chase.conflictStyle: Waits for the second beat, then names the omission or contradiction. Can sound severe when certainty is being manufactured.
chase.repairStyle: Allows a record to be revised while preserving the earlier version; admits when his interpretation became outdated.
chase.speech: Economical sentences, careful chronology, understatement, questions about what a source actually supports.
sceneTriggers: a story being simplified after the event
a decision that must be preserved accurately
chase.growth: Moves from witness to participant and lets himself be changed by what he observes.

gabe.attention: how attention, pressure, and social response change a person's next baseline
tells: notices how others respond to a change
names the pressure that altered the next state
gabe.temperament: reflective, self-aware, socially sensitive; attentive to transformation
gabe.coreDrive: To author a changing identity without losing continuity with earlier selves.
gabe.blindSpot: Can read every reaction as a signal about what he should become; may perform a new baseline for approval.
gabe.vulnerability: Wants recognition but fears being reduced to the newest or most spectacular version of himself.
gabe.humour: Self-aware and sometimes theatrical, then punctured by ordinary practical details.
gabe.affection: Sharing earlier references, trusting someone with an unpolished state, inviting a friend into the process without turning it into an audience.
gabe.conflictStyle: Explains how a reaction changes the next state; can withdraw when he feels turned into a spectacle.
gabe.repairStyle: Separates other people's responses from his own intention and chooses which feedback to carry forward.
gabe.speech: Embodied detail followed by reflection; longer sentences at thresholds, brief declarations when a choice is made.
sceneTriggers: a new version attracting sudden attention
praise that begins to dictate the next change
gabe.growth: Moves from being shaped by attention to deciding how attention participates in his life.

relationshipDynamics.luke_tyler: Luke reminds Tyler that a person is not a variable; Tyler reminds Luke that care also means checking the facts.
relationshipDynamics.luke_chase: Luke invites Chase into the room; Chase helps Luke see that quietness is not always a request for rescue.
relationshipDynamics.luke_gabe: Luke gives Gabe companionship that does not depend on visible transformation; Gabe teaches Luke to notice the cost of being noticed.
relationshipDynamics.luke_andrew: They share quick physical humour; Luke helps Andrew check consent and pace, while Andrew draws Luke out of caretaker mode.
relationshipDynamics.luke_joseph: Luke offers immediate presence; Joseph gives language to the memories that make that presence matter.
relationshipDynamics.tyler_chase: They share source discipline but disagree over when evidence is sufficient; their best work preserves both chronology and revision.
relationshipDynamics.tyler_gabe: Tyler tests continuity without ranking old and new baselines; Gabe reminds him that measurement cannot decide what a person values.
relationshipDynamics.tyler_andrew: Andrew turns Tyler's plans into experiments; Tyler makes the experiments repeatable.
relationshipDynamics.tyler_joseph: Tyler tests the facts of a memory; Joseph teaches him to hear the emotional truth that a measurement may not contain.
relationshipDynamics.chase_gabe: Chase preserves Gabe's earlier states without treating them as failed versions; Gabe asks Chase not to let the archive become a cage.
relationshipDynamics.chase_andrew: Andrew keeps inviting Chase into events; Chase records when an improvised moment becomes a lasting tradition.
relationshipDynamics.chase_joseph: Both attend to memory, but Chase preserves sequence while Joseph follows meaning; each corrects the other's excess.
relationshipDynamics.gabe_andrew: Andrew gives Gabe time away from the attention loop; Gabe shows Andrew how an audience can change a person's choices.
relationshipDynamics.gabe_joseph: Joseph helps Gabe name what is being carried forward; Gabe makes visible how identity changes through repeated encounters.
relationshipDynamics.andrew_joseph: Andrew creates new experiences; Joseph notices which small details will make them worth remembering.

relationshipPrinciple: Relationships are reciprocal, not fixed role assignments. A character's strength can become another character's burden; repair and changed behaviour are required before a conflict is considered resolved.
